To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
obesity due to high-fat Western diet consumption increases tumor growth in mouse xenograft models of human colon adenocarcinoma.
obesity due to a HFWD accelerates human colon cancer growth in two different mouse models, and this may be related to changes in inflammatory-associated genes in the epididymal adipose tissue.
obesity, insulin resistance, and inflammation contribute to increased and accelerated tumor progression in a mouse model of human colon cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the mechanisms that link obesity to colon cancer.
the effects of obesity on the development and progression of colon cancer.
the effect of obesity on colon cancer growth and the underlying mechanisms that may contribute to this phenomenon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consumption of an HFD increases tumor growth in mouse xenograft models of human colon cancers, and this is mediated by increased inflammation in adipose tissue and tumor tissue.
obesity and the HFWD-induced insulin resistance contribute to the growth and progression of colon cancer.
high-fat Western diet-fed obese mice have significantly increased and accelerated tumor xenograft growth compared with low-fat Western diet–fed lean mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity and the consumption of a high fat diet are associated with an increase in tumor growth and tumor metastases.

obesity, as induced by a high-fat Western-style diet, promotes the growth of human colonic adenocarcinomas, and that leptin, c-Jun N-terminal protein kinase, and monocyte chemonattractant protein-1 are potential mediators of this effect.
obesity and insulin resistance due to the consumption and HFWD can lead to increased tumor growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obesity, insulin resistance, and leptin resistance may be important in the development of colon cancer.
obesity is a major factor in tumor growth.
obesity is a significant risk factor for colon cancer and that it should be taken into account during the design of colon cancer clinical trials.
